correctness.rationale: At n=2,3,4 direct calculation leaves only 3, phi(3)=phi(4)=2. For n>=5 let e be the even member; Omega(e)<=2 implies e=2r with r an odd prime, so phi(e)=r-1. The neighboring odd integer must be prime s, odd prime square s², or product ab of distinct odd primes. Equality phi(o)=r-1 then e=o±1 contradicts consecutiveness for o=s; for o=s² gives (s-1)^2=0 or discriminant -8; for o=ab gives (a-2)(b-2)=1 or -1, impossible with a<b odd primes. Every factorization shape and both neighbor orientations are checked, proving the unrestricted statement. Independent exact totient and Omega sieves through n=160000 returned only n=3; finite scan is corroborative, not the source of the universal assertion.
residual_risks: Independent numerical checks cover only a finite range; the exact unbounded conclusion depends on its full factorization or three-arc proof.
